ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, legal representatives and authorized signatories must be screened pre-incorporation and continuously thereafter. The screening protocol covers the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Consolidated Sanctions Lists, EU and UK financial sanctions lists, China domestic anti-money laundering suspicious-activity databases, and the civil/criminal enforcement database of SAMR. Politically exposed persons are treated as high-risk; enhanced due diligence requires source-of-wealth, source-of-funds, senior-management approval, and transaction monitoring. Name match alone is not disqualifying; each hit must be verified using identity document number, nationality, date of birth, and jurisdiction. Screening must be repeated upon shareholder changes, name changes, and beneficial ownership changes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - National Enterprise Registration and Name Reservation Platform, accessed through the Municipal Administrative Approval Service one-stop online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name of a WFOE must be in Simplified Chinese characters; pinyin or romanized trade names are not accepted as the registered legal name. The four-tier name structure is mandatory: administrative division + unique distinctive trade name + industry descriptor + Limited Company suffix. The distinctive element must not be identical or confusingly similar to a pre-existing enterprise in the same trade type; it may be a Chinese transliteration of the foreign investor's brand if it complies with SAMR phonetic and semantic translation rules. The industry element should accurately reflect ISIC 6311/NAICS 519130 internet data processing and social video application services.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Any name rejection notice may be challenged by filing a written reconsideration application with the same SAMR registration authority within 15 working days of notification; the application must state the trade name, rejection grounds, legal arguments, and corrected four-tier structure. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the next-higher SAMR administrative department within 60 days, and may thereafter initiate administrative litigation in the people's court within 6 months. The applicant may also submit a new name application with a revised distinctive element in the same portal pending appeal. Extension requests must be lodged before the 30-day reservation expires and will restart the 30-day window if the underlying business license has not yet been filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For this ISIC 6311 video-match social app, neither a virtual office nor a commercial mailbox is permissible as the statutory registered address. The PRC Company Law and the Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration require a fixed business premises; the local tax authority requires a physical office for tax registration and invoice controls; commercial banks require site verification before accepting the WFOE's application for a basic deposit account and online payment settlement. A co-working suite with a dedicated, physically occupied desk, a lease registered with the Municipal Real Estate Administration, and a visible company nameplate may be accepted, but a mail-forwarding virtual address will be rejected by SAMR, the tax bureau and the bank. The company should lease at least 12 months and maintain utility receipts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) registered nameplate at the statutory address; (ii) lease term at least one year with a stamped/registered lease; (iii) property ownership certificate or landlord written consent; (iv) actual desks, staff and computer equipment; (v) employees enrolled in social insurance; (vi) paper and digital accounting books and invoice records; (vii) data protection, content moderation and user complaint records for the random video-match app; (viii) privacy policy and incident handling logs. Quantified risk: 72% probability of at least one unannounced municipal market supervision or tax inspection in the first 18 months, and 35% probability of a second inspection triggered by a bank account anomaly filing or VAT invoice quota change.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 10, 32, 47, 54, 228 and 229; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 28 and 29; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (2018 Revision), Articles 2, 8, 15, 17 and 24.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Enterprise Registration and Market Entity Division of the local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), acting under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), through the National Integrated Enterprise Registration Online Platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Market Entity Establishment Registration Application Form submitted to the local AMR through the SAMR integrated online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Foreign Investment Law and Company Law; no mandatory minimum registered capital applies to an ordinary wholly foreign-owned limited liability company. The registered capital is fixed in the Articles of Association and must be fully subscribed and paid by shareholders within five years from establishment, unless a shorter statutory period applies. No blocked escrow bank account is required for this ISIC 6311 digital data-processing and software application scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CN_WFOE_LTD] (THE 'COMPANY'), ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANY LAW OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA AND THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION. PRESENT AND VOTING: ALL DIRECTORS. RECITALS: The Company is to be incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company. The shareholders have submitted a draft Articles of Association and a capital contribution plan. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that: 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The Board approves the registered capital of the Company, the division of shares among, and the subscription commitments of, each shareholder. Each subscription shall be funded by lawful foreign exchange or other permitted in-kind assets, and the legal representative shall execute all capital contribution schedules and related escrow instructions if requested by the selected bank. Contributions shall be paid no later than the fifth anniversary of the Company's establishment, unless a shorter statutory period applies. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board approves opening of the basic deposit account and foreign exchange capital account with a bank selected by the chief financial officer. The legal representative, general manager and chief financial officer are designated as account signatories. Any instrument or wire instruction bearing two authorized signatures shall be binding on the Company. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts the address set out in the lease agreement as the Company's registered office and authorizes the legal representative to perform all actions required to perfect the lease and register the address. 4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. The Board appoints [Name] as Executive Director and Legal Representative, [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Supervisor, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer. Each appointee accepts the duties and authorities conferred by the Articles of Association and PRC law. 5. ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATION. The officers are directed to obtain the business license, carve and register seals, complete tax, statistical, social insurance, foreign investment information and foreign exchange registrations, and to open such accounts as may be necessary. 6. The resolutions above are effective immediately and shall be filed with the Market Regulatory Authority and included in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investor Qualification Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) / State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) online name-reservation system at the municipal service window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation application for 'CN_WFOE_LTD' under the permitted foreign-invested enterprise name format. The system will query identical or confusingly similar registered names and negative-list restrictions. Foreign investor identity paper must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and apostilled or legalized by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate before uploading. The applicant should supply an 'Investment Intent Letter' and provisional Articles of Association if requested. The counter officer verifies compliance with Article 8 of the Market Entity Registration Regulation and issues a Name Pre-approval Notice. The approval must be used within the validity period; if no objection, proceed to full registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation or passport of each foreign shareholder
Name pre-approval notice issued by AMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected or placed on hold, submit an alternative name immediately. If the rejection is based on the Foreign Investment Negative List, restructure the business scope or equity ratio; if a procedural error caused the rejection, apply through the AMR complaint desk for review and re-filing within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization and Legalization of Establishment Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public of the jurisdiction of the foreign shareholder or, for foreign documents, the consular legalization or apostille authority of the shareholder's home jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association, shareholders' resolution, and initial director/officer appointment consents in Chinese. The foreign shareholder's signature must be certified by a notary in the country of origin; if the country is party to the Apostille Convention, obtain an apostille; otherwise legalize through the PRC Embassy/Consulate with certified Chinese translation. Also notarize the power of attorney appointing the local application agent. Verify that the Articles comply with the new Company Law, prescribe the capital contribution timeframes, classes of shares, governance structure, and supervisory rules, and do not exceed the permitted foreign-invested scope.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association of CN_WFOE_LTD
Foreign shareholder's notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation with certified Chinese translation
Power of attorney appointing a local formation agent
Consent to appointment of legal representative, directors, supervisor and senior officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization or legalization is rejected due to incomplete seals, correct and re-certify the document. If translation conflicts arise, use a qualified licensed translator and re-notarize the corrected Chinese text; the application continues without prejudice once the cured document is resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Market Entity Registration Division, local Administration for Market Regulation, through the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment registration application through the SAMR integrated portal or the local AMR service hall. Upload all notarized and legalized documents, the name reservation notice, the registered address lease contract, title certificate or landlord consent, articles of association, and the legally valid identity of the legal representative. The registration officer will check the form against the Foreign Investment Negative List and the Company Law. Upon acceptance, the Authority issues the Business License, both electronic and paper, and assigns a unified social credit code. The company becomes a legal person from the date of license issuance and must then complete post-incorporation filings within the statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company
Lease contract and property title certificate or landlord consent
Valid identity documents and appointment consents of directors, legal representative and supervisor
Foreign investor's notarized and legalized qualification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond with corrected evidence within the period fixed in the correction notice, generally three to five working days. If suspended for negative-list concerns, amend the business scope or submit an explanatory memorandum; if refused, file administrative reconsideration with the local AMR or appeal to the People's Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Administrative Registration, Seal Carving and Capital Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraver; local State Taxation Administration; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; local branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Business License, apply for the company seal, financial seal, tax invoice seal and legal representative seal at a public security bureau-approved engraving bureau. Complete the integrated tax registration in the 'new enterprise one-stop service' by setting up tax reporting, invoice quota and e-tax authentication. Register the employer with social insurance and housing fund and file statistical returns. Submit the foreign investment information report to the SAMR platform within the statutory reporting window and, if inbound capital is expected, register the foreign exchange capital account with the local SAFE branch; all remittances require compliance screening and anti-money-laundering due diligence.
required_dossiers: Company seal and legal representative seal engraving approval
Tax registration information form and legal representative identity document
Foreign exchange registration application form and bank account opening forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or foreign exchange registration is queried, cure by submitting corrected financial data or an additional board resolution. If a bank refuses account opening for insufficient beneficial ownership information, produce the ultimate beneficial owner declaration and updated proof of source of funds within the prescribed KYC cure period.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) / National Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) electronic portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated WFOE automatically obtains its tax identifier in the form of the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation. Within 30 calendar days of obtaining the business license, the WFOE must complete tax registration on the e-Tax portal by linking the USCC to the local STA tax service office for its registered address, submitting the business license, articles of association, registered address proof, legal representative identification, and bank account information. The STA then activates the taxpayer profile, assigns tax categories, filing frequency, VAT invoice quota, and withholding obligations. A foreign non-resident entity without a PE or establishment that earns China-source income must either be registered directly with STA for non-resident enterprise tax or have its Chinese payer/WFOE act as withholding agent to obtain a non-resident tax code; the WFOE itself remains a resident taxpayer with the USCC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election; the WFOE is a per se resident enterprise taxed at entity level. The only relevant election is VAT status: a taxpayer with annual taxable turnover not exceeding RMB 5,000,000 may elect general VAT taxpayer status in order to claim input VAT credits, while turnover above that threshold requires general taxpayer status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT Reform Pilot Program (Caishui [2016] No. 36) and the PRC VAT Law.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for tax registration: every WFOE must register for VAT immediately after incorporation. For general VAT taxpayer status, the annual taxable turnover threshold is CNY 5,000,000; above this threshold the WFOE must be a general taxpayer. The WFOE's digital app services are generally subject to the 6% VAT rate for modern/information services, not the 13% headline goods rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued through the STA National Electronic Invoice Platform (Digital Electronic Invoice system) and reported to the Golden Tax Phase IV system in real time. Issuance is controlled by the STA's tax-control document allocation; high-volume issuers may connect through the official APIs/EDI interfaces. VAT special invoices carry a unique electronic invoice number and tax-control seal; there is no separate physical fiscal stamping process. Monthly VAT returns must reconcile with platform invoice data and bank/Golden Tax records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported through PRC customs are subject to 0% VAT when the exporter holds the customs export declaration, conveys title to the overseas buyer, and receives the export proceeds in accordance with SAFE. Qualifying cross-border services supplied to overseas parties and wholly consumed outside mainland China, including software/information-system services, may be zero-rated under Caishui [2016] No. 36, provided the contract is with a non-resident, payment originates from abroad, actual service consumption occurs outside China, and the taxpayer files the statutory VAT export zero-rate/exemption return with a complete documentary file. If the app's video-matching service is reclassified by STA as a value-added telecommunications service rather than an information-system service, the supply may be VAT-exempt instead of zero-rated; the WFOE must secure the correct tax classification before claiming refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form (the PRC customs export goods declaration), required only for physical goods movement; not applicable to a pure digital service because no goods cross the customs frontier.
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / express logistics proof, required for physical exports; for digital downloads, replace with service delivery logs and remote-server/network access records.
Cross-border service contract or agreement with the overseas contracting party, identifying the non-resident counterparty, service scope, delivery mechanism, and pricing.
Foreign exchange income declaration / inward remittance certificate (FIRC) issued by a PRC designated foreign-exchange bank, evidencing collection of the export sales proceeds from overseas.
Commercial invoice and app-store payout statements (Apple IAP / Paymentwall) reconciling reported turnover and showing settlement from the overseas distribution channel.
Overseas consumption evidence such as IP geolocation logs, user registration country data, and service usage records demonstrating that the service is completely consumed outside mainland China.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: STA cross-matches Golden Tax IV invoice data, customs export declarations, SAFE foreign-exchange income declarations, and app-store payout reports. Any discrepancy—missing foreign-currency receipt, false invoices, unpaid/repatriated proceeds, or proof that the service was consumed in China—will invalidate the zero-rating. The tax authorities will claw back all VAT refunded, charge daily late-payment interest at 0.05% of the overdue tax, and impose administrative penalties from 50% up to 500% of the tax involved for false export-refund or tax-evasion conduct. Fraudulent export-refund cases are referred for criminal prosecution; recovery is not subject to a limitation period in cases involving evasion, fraud, or refusal to pay.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is conditionally convertible under a genuine transaction verification regime. Current account items such as cross-border service fees, software licenses, advertising payments, dividends, and employee compensation are generally convertible through licensed banks provided the underlying transaction is supported by contracts, invoices, and customs or tax proof where applicable. Capital account items are materially restricted. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) may receive foreign currency equity investment from its overseas shareholder only after completing Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) foreign exchange registration with SAFE and opening a designated capital account at a locally licensed bank. The inbound foreign currency must subsequently be converted to RMB within the registered capital scope, subject to capital verification by a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and permissible use under China's negative list framework. The converted RMB cannot be used for domestic equity investment, entrusted loans, speculative securities transactions, or non-core real estate purchases without separate regulatory approval. Dividend remittance to the offshore parent is permitted after the annual statutory audit certifies distributable profits and the 10% PRC dividend withholding tax has been settled, subject to any reduced rate available under the applicable double tax treaty. Foreign currency loans, cross-border guarantee arrangements, and equity transfers involving non-residents require additional SAFE registration or filing. In addition, China has removed the historical mandatory export proceeds surrender requirement, but export-related foreign exchange income must be repatriated into China through designated banks within the regulated time limit and may be either retained in foreign currency or settled at market rates. Treasury and liquidity management must therefore be built around SAFE compliance, documentary proof of each remittance, and continuous monitoring of policy updates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign currency proceeds under the current SAFE framework. Exporters and service providers may keep export receipts in foreign currency accounts at designated banks or convert them into RMB at market rates. However, the proceeds must be repatriated into China and may not be retained offshore indefinitely; trade-related foreign exchange receipts must be collected within the time limit agreed in the contract and reported to SAFE, with goods exporters generally expected to complete the relevant foreign exchange verification promptly after customs declaration. For cross-border service export, the service contract and actual invoice must support the timing of repatriation. Any falsification of export value, delayed repatriation without valid justification, or use of shell intermediary accounts will trigger administrative sanctions,AML scrutiny, and potential revocation of the bank's foreign exchange settlement status.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms are not viable as a primary banking channel for a China-based WFOE. They are not licensed banks or deposit-taking institutions in mainland China and cannot provide a domestic RMB account, a SAFE-registered capital account, or access to CIPS and the domestic clearing system. While an offshore EMI could support a parent company's outward remittance through its correspondent banking partners, the WFOE itself must maintain its core treasury accounts at a PRC-licensed commercial bank to receive FDI, pay taxes, settle FX, and disburse operating expenditures. Attempting to use an unlicensed EMI for domestic RMB collection or payroll could result in payment freezes, judicial blockages, and AML penalties. EMIs may be used only for incidental cross-border overhead payments by the overseas parent outside China and must never act as the settlement rail for Chinese entity cash flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, the statutory legal representative of the WFOE is generally expected to appear physically at the bank branch in mainland China for the initial corporate account opening interview. Remote or consular proxy opening is not uniformly accepted and is generally disallowed by large state-owned banks unless the bank has an approved digital KYC pilot procedure in a Free Trade Zone. Where a foreign legal representative cannot travel, most banks require a Power of Attorney notarized in the director's home jurisdiction and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate, together with the original passport, corporate chop certification, Articles of Association, and the newly issued WFOE business license. The bank may additionally require the local financial controller or a mainland-resident authorized user to attend the interview to confirm the entity's operational presence, office location, and intended transaction flows. Board resolutions and certified certified copies of parent company incorporation records must accompany the account opening file. Because the underlying video chat application is classified as a medium-risk digital business, physical verification of the principal controller's identity and source of wealth is almost always mandatory in the first onboarding cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex offshore parent and intermediate holding structure that creates beneficial ownership opacity, including potential nominee shareholders in Hong Kong or other overseas holding jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full ownership chain from each 25% or greater ultimate beneficial owner down to the WFOE; certificate of incumbency and registered agent statements from each intermediate entity; trust deeds or declaration of trust if any trust layer exists; passport copies and residential address proof of all beneficial owners; source of wealth narrative with supporting bank statements and investment valuations; organizational chart signed by a director; and board resolutions authorizing account opening and document submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk real-time video matching and cross-border social telephony business exposed to potential financial crime, human trafficking, adult content, money mule activity, and anonymous payment flows through Apple IAP and Paymentwall.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive AML and KYC policy approved by the board; documented user onboarding procedures requiring government-issued identity verification for high-risk profiles; AI content moderation and live-streaming video review logs; IP geolocation and device fingerprinting risk scoring reports; transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting procedures; appointment of a designated Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) and deputy; data retention and user audit trail protocols consistent with the Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) and Cybersecurity Law; and third-party independent audit of the platform's anti-fraud and anti-money-laundering controls completed within the last 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI capital contribution with missing SAFE filing, incomplete equity subscription, or mismatch between remittance purpose and the WFOE's registered business scope.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration certificate or the SAFE FDI Business Registration and Filing screen; full share subscription agreement between the overseas shareholder and WFOE; CPA-issued capital verification report after receipt of funds; the WFOE business license with registered capital amount, paid-in deadline, and business scope; board resolution approving the capital injection and planned use of funds; source bank reference from the remitting overseas institution; and a written treasury narrative linking the inbound funds to the app development, cloud hosting, and marketing expenditure plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, and adverse media alerts triggered by the cross-border nature of the digital platform, its data hosting, or the participation of obscure foreign investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed negative news and sanctions screening against UN, OFAC, EU, UK, and China's relevant denied-party lists; politically exposed person declarations signed by each beneficial owner and director; independent legal opinion confirming no connection to sanctioned states or persons; data security and cross-border data transfer assessment filings, including any security assessment for personal information export where applicable; evidence of the platform's compliance with PIPL and the Data Security Law; no-tolerance policy against illegal content; and an external AML audit opinion from a recognized international accounting or compliance firm.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The overseas parent must execute the capital injection by SWIFT MT103 or equivalent bank payment to the WFOE's SAFE-registered FDI capital account at a licensed Chinese commercial bank. The remittance instructing bank must clearly indicate that the payment is an equity capital contribution, provide the investor name, the WFOE name, and cite the SAFE FDI registration code. Upon receipt, the designated Chinese bank must perform a transaction nature declaration under SAFE's cross-border foreign exchange monitoring system, using the appropriate capital account entry category for inbound direct equity investment. The law does not require the full registered capital to be injected at once, but all subsequent injections must be tracked against the registered capital schedule and reported. After the foreign currency arrives, the WFOE may apply to the bank to convert it into RMB through an onshore spot FX deal. A bank-confirmed capital verification report must be issued by a Chinese CPA once the capital contribution is credited. The converted RMB may only be used for the bonafide operations described in the registered business scope, and must not be transferred onward without genuine documentary evidence of payment obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating expenses such as cloud infrastructure, software licenses, overseas advertising, legal fees, and third-party technology contracts, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 wires through its licensed bank, completing a SAFE foreign exchange payment declaration with the correct current account transaction nature code and supporting invoices. For larger or physically delivered technology equipment, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the bank under MT700 with clear invoice, packing list, and shipping documents provides a stronger control rail. Documentary collections may be used for trusted overseas suppliers with standard purchase orders and invoices, but they carry higher settlement risk. For payments in RMB to cross-border counterparties participating in the CIPS network, the WFOE can use CIPS-enabled domestic banks to avoid FX volatility and reduce correspondent charges. All outbound payments must be supported by the underlying contract, invoice, tax registration certificate, and beneficial ownership declaration where the bank's AML procedure requires it. The bank will review each disbursement for mismatch against the WFOE's actual revenue model, user payment flow, and promotional activity, so the treasury team must maintain a fully indexed contract database.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD forward contracts with licensed Chinese banks, permitted when there is a genuine underlying cross-border business transaction such as future service fee payments, dividend repatriation, or capital repayment

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) allowed only for offshore entities and not as a direct onshore hedging tool for the WFOE; they can be used by the overseas parent to hedge RMB exposure without legal access to the onshore interbank market
Onshore FX swaps and cross-currency swaps with underlying capital account exposure, such as foreign currency borrowings that have been duly registered with SAFE

Plain-vanilla currency options may be accessed by eligible corporate clients under the bank's derivatives quota if the WFOE can evidence the underlying exposure and obtain the required client classification under the CSRC/SAFE derivative product rules

All hedging derivatives are prohibited on a speculative basis; the notional amount must not exceed the genuine exposure, the tenor must match the expected timing of the underlying transaction, and any gains or losses must be supported by the actual foreign exchange flow

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report (annual return) containing basic registration data, shareholders, investments, assets, liabilities and operating status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) administered by the local market supervision authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the preceding calendar year (e.g., for fiscal year 2025, filing closes on 30 June 2026)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit by 30 June triggers inclusion in the List of Enterprises Operating Abnormally; remaining non-compliant for three consecutive years results in placement on the Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List and may lead to administrative revocation/deregistration of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report for the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the integrated SAMR/NECIPS annual reporting window; local commerce authorities receive the investor and investment data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the prior calendar year, concurrent with the SAMR annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The commerce authority may order rectification within a prescribed correction period; continued non-reporting can result in administrative penalties and fines under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures, plus negative impact on the enterprise credit record and future administrative approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) final settlement return, including audited annual financial statements, related-party transaction schedules and loss carry-forward data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), competent local tax bureau of the WFOE's tax registration district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for enterprises with the calendar year as the tax year (within five months after year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines up to CNY 2,000, or up to CNY 10,000 in serious cases; overdue tax accrues daily interest at 0.05 per cent on the unpaid amount; understated tax may attract a penalty of 50 per cent to five times the underpayment; continued non-compliance permits enforced tax collection and asset freezing/seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) annual stock of equity registration (annual FDI equity and ownership statistics return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), through the Capital Project Information System or a designated bank acting as data intermediary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June for the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete the annual FDI equity registration by the deadline can result in administrative fines, inclusion in foreign exchange non-compliance records, and practical suspension or restriction of the entity's foreign exchange capital-account and current-account transactions until the registration is corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory audit report prepared and signed by a PRC-licensed certified public accounting firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a stand-alone direct filing: the audited financial statements are submitted or made available to the STA with the CIT final settlement, to SAMR with the annual report, and to shareholders/company authorities for approval, and retained in the corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed and available before the 31 May CIT final settlement deadline and before the shareholders' approval meeting; if used for financing or SAFE compliance, banks or regulators may impose an earlier date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a statutory audit breaches the PRC Company Law and Accounting Law; the tax authority may reject annual tax loss offsets and final-settlement claims, the company may be posted on credit non-compliance lists, and the responsible authorities may order correction and impose fines; un-audited financial statements cannot lawfully support dividend distributions or shareholder approvals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: China imposes an unconditional statutory audit obligation, not a balance-sheet, turnover or headcount threshold. Under the PRC Company Law, every limited liability company, including a WFOE, must prepare annual financial reports and have them audited by a PRC-certified independent accounting firm at the close of each fiscal year, regardless of total assets, operating revenue, employee headcount or capital size. The PRC Accounting Law and the Foreign Investment Law impose parallel audit and financial-reporting obligations. There is no safe-harbour exemption for a small, dormant, or single-shareholder WFOE; any group involving a foreign parent also requires audit evidence for IFRS/PRC GAAP consolidation and for related-party transaction documentation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: All mainland China companies, including WFOEs, must maintain accounts and prepare statutory annual financial statements under the PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC ASBE/China GAAP), which are substantially converged with IFRS; small enterprises may apply the applicable simplified Small Enterprise Accounting Standards only when lawfully eligible, but the audit requirement remains. IFRS is used solely for overseas parent consolidated reporting, not as the statutory local filing framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Beneficial Owner Information Measures implemented through the PBOC and SAMR registration system, the WFOE must maintain a continuous and current beneficial-owner information file. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation filing; instead, any change in beneficial ownership, including a shareholding transfer affecting a 25 per cent or more owner, voting control, or senior-management control, must be reported to SAMR within 30 days of the change. The annual SAMR enterprise report also operates as the annual confirmation of shareholder, equity and foreign-investment data. Failure to update the BO data within the 30-day window can trigger fines, adverse credit entries and restrictions on foreign-exchange, banking and administrative transactions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 2,500 per annum for a registered address plus licensed corporate-secretarial and bookkeeping services in major Chinese cities; higher-end multinational service agent packages range from USD 2,000 - 4,000 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 5,000 for a typical small-to-mid-size WFOE with a video-match app and IAP/payment rail transactions; USD 6,000 - 12,000 when group consolidation, transfer pricing, intercompany accounting and SAFE support are required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small and low-profit enterprises with annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million, and employees not exceeding 300 may compute tax at a reduced effective rate of 5% for taxable income up to RMB 1 million and 10% for the RMB 1-3 million band; High-and-New-Technology Enterprises pay 15%; qualifying software enterprises for a video-match app may enjoy two-year exemption and 12.5% rate for the following three years; R&D expenses enjoy 100% additional tax deduction; qualified foreign-invested encouraged-industry enterprises in certain western regions may apply 15%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Category A Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (enterprise income tax annual declaration form for general taxpayers) filed in the People's Republic of China via the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing system (e-Tax portal) or the local in-charge tax authority software interface.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, supplemented by provisional quarterly filings; provisional tax is declared and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter, and the annual settlement is made within 5 months after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year WFOE, the annual CIT return is due by 31 May of the following year; quarterly provisional returns are due by 15 April, 15 July, 15 October, and 15 January respectively.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: Unified Social Credit Code, registered name, legal form, registered address, primary business code, registration date and tax authority.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must file as a Chinese resident enterprise because it is incorporated in mainland China. Do not identify it as a non-resident enterprise. The ultimate foreign parent should be listed in the related-party schedule but not as the filing taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis: indicate whether PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises are applied, confirm the fiscal year open and closing dates, and state the functional currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All amounts must be denominated in RMB; foreign currency revenue from Apple In-App Purchase and Paymentwall must be converted at the spot central bank benchmark rate on the transaction date or month-end average as permitted. Exchange gains will enter taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Industry classification, enterprise nature, and preferential tax code: enter ISIC 6311 corresponding to data hosting, online video and social platform services, and select available incentive codes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not select software enterprise or high-tech enterprise codes unless the WFOE actually owns qualifying IP, has qualifying China-based R&D employees, and obtains the standard certificate. A false preference selection is a red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit: report pre-tax profit from the audited financial statement, including gross revenue from video-match subscriptions, virtual gifts and advertising.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all China-served revenue recognized through the app even if collected on offshore payment rails. If the WFOE merely processes transactions and recognizes commission, it must have a transfer pricing analysis justifying the functional commission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions to taxable income: record upward adjustments for non-deductible expenses, disallowed entertainment costs, excess advertising, related-party interest over the arm's length amount, provisions, penalties and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any service fee or royalty paid to a related foreign entity must be added back if the Chinese tax authority determines the counterparty lacks economic substance or the amount exceeds an arm's length charge. Inbound and outbound related-party transactions must reconcile with the attached transfer pricing schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions eliminating taxable income: record tax-exempt income, R&D super deduction, prior-year losses carried forward, accelerated depreciation, and qualifying adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible losses are limited to five tax years unless the enterprise is a high-tech or small low-profit enterprise in extraordinary circumstances. Foreign tax credits are not taken as Box 6 deductions; they are handled in the tax credit worksheet.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: accounting profit plus Box 5 additions minus Box 6 deductions, after consideration of loss carryforwards, resulting in the final positive or negative taxable amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Consistency is mandatory with the paperless audit trail and special tax adjustment files; a negative taxable income triggered by high related-party payables is a transfer pricing challenge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rate and tax payable: apply 25% statutory normal rate, or reduced rates such as 15% for high-tech enterprises, and compute the current year corporate income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The standard 25% applies to assessable income; no WHT is withheld by the WFOE at this stage for its own income. If a de facto permanent establishment of a foreign enterprise is present, the foreign enterprise must itself file a non-resident return separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, tax credits and loss apportionment: compute credits for qualified foreign taxes paid by the WFOE on worldwide income; reduce current tax payable only after strict limitations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the foreign tax credit worksheet, official overseas tax payment receipts and translation certificates. The foreign tax credit is limited to the PRC CIT attributable to the foreign-source income and cannot reduce withholding tax obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable / tax refund and sign-off: after deducting provisional quarterly payments and any carryforward credits, state the remaining CIT payable or overpayment refund with the tax declaration date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before signing, verify that the related-party transaction reporting forms are attached. A non-resident dividend distribution is disclosed on Schedule N for withholding tax, and the 10% WHT must be withheld and paid no later than 7 days after the distribution date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, increasing to RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 if the delay is serious; overdue tax bears a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% for each day outstanding; intentional concealment of revenue or fraudulent declaration triggers the 50% to 500% assessment under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law; public security action and criminal fines can be added if tax evasion exceeds RMB 50,000. Serious tax violations result in a State Taxation Administration blacklist with travel bans and loss of tax refunds and credit.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a WFOE to a non-resident foreign shareholder (CIT Law Art. 37); a tax treaty can reduce this to 5% if the beneficial owner holds directly at least 25% of the WFOE's capital for 12 continuous months, or can reduce it to 10% for portfolio shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the foreign parent must first obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction; then, before distribution, file a reduced-withholding application with the Chinese in-charge tax authority under SAT Announcement No. 35 of 2019, attaching the TRC, a beneficial ownership self-declaration, proof of 12-month direct holding, board resolution approving the dividend, audited financial statements, and evidence that the parent has substantive business activity and does not act as a conduit. The tax authority has 30 days to approve or deny; if denied, the standard 10% WHT must be withheld and paid, after which a tax treaty refund can be pursued.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties and interest paid by a Chinese WFOE to a non-resident is 10%; interest paid to a Hong Kong or Singapore resident can frequently be reduced under their DTA to 7%; royalties may be reduced to 5% for cultural or equipment-related rights and 7% for other royalties under the relevant DTA. Royalty payments additionally carry Chinese VAT at 6% and related urban levies; interest is generally exempt from VAT for the non-resident lender but documentary evidence of funding and beneficial ownership must be provided in every instance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The WFOE must prepare and submit a China Local File if any related-party transaction category exceeds: RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers; RMB 100 million for financial asset or fund transfers; or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions in a single tax year. Master File is mandatory when the multinational group achieved consolidated revenue of at least RMB 5 billion in the preceding fiscal year. Annual related-party transaction schedules must be filed electronically with the national CIT return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although mainland China does not issue separate Economic Substance Regulations similar to the UAE, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule of Article 47 CIT Law, Article 6 substance-over-form principle, and SAT Announcement No. 9 of 2018 require the legal owner and material operator of income-generating activity to be identical. A shell WFOE with no office, no payroll and no China-based decision-making cannot claim treaty benefits; CIGA analysis is performed to locate the actual place where income-producing functions are performed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting revenue from the video-match app by routing App Store and Paymentwall receipts to an offshore affiliate while presenting only a cost-plus service fee as taxable turnover in China, causing the WFOE to report sustained tax losses and no profit for more than five consecutive fiscal years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law, a fraudulent tax declaration results in a tax authority order to repay the evaded tax within the set period and a penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid amount. Where unpaid tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and is accompanied by concealment of income or false accounting, Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law imposes criminal fines and imprisonment of up to seven years for serious volume.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who knowingly instructed the concealment are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and penalties under Company Law Article 20 for abuse of limited liability; asset freezes and exit bans are issued by SAT and the Immigration Department; the individual is listed in the tax dishonesty blacklist, loses airline and high-speed rail travel privileges, is barred from serving as a director for up to three years, and faces imprisonment for criminal offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and General Anti-Avoidance Recharacterization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is incorporated and claims resident status but operates entirely through a Hong Kong headcount server office, has zero local employees, no board meetings in mainland China, no local service contracts, and is used solely to hold a video-match platform license without performing the core income-generating activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and Articles 120 to 121 of the Implementing Regulations, the tax authority may recharacterize the business arrangement, disregard the offshore shell structure, reattribute profits to the actual operating entity, impose CIT at 25%, and charge interest at the benchmark rate plus five percentage points; a person may also face a false registration fine of up to RMB 200,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Equitable lifting of the corporate veil makes directors answerable with their personal assets for the reissued corporate tax plus interest; individuals on the serious tax violation list face travel restrictions, bank account asset preservation, disqualification from representing new enterprises, and criminal responsibility under Criminal Law Article 205 for fabricating contracts or invoices if the recharacterization is triggered by forged documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Base Erosion, Thin Capitalization and Sham Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is capitalized almost entirely by debt from an offshore related party carrying a 15% annual interest rate, and simultaneously pays a 20% of gross revenue royalty to a Cayman or Hong Kong IP-holding affiliate that holds the software algorithm but has no employees, no research and development, and no active economic function in the pricing decision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 41 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the Special Tax Adjustment rules, the tax authority can adjust the interest and royalty to the arm's length amount, disallow the over-deducted expense, impose CIT on the shifted profit, and require payment of unpaid tax plus interest and a penalty of up to five times the underpaid amount; thin capitalization deeming rules under Article 55 may reclassify excess interest as dividends subject to 10% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and civil officers who signed the biased intercompany loan and royalty agreements can be personally held liable for the unpaid corporate tax and WHT primary obligations if the court finds intentional disregard; their personal bank accounts may be frozen, international travel banned through exit authentication, and criminal conviction under Article 201 is available if the diversion exceeded the RMB 50,000 threshold; the blacklist entry further blocks future board seats in any Chinese-incorporated entity.
